title: Understanding Bias and Variance
text: Bias refers to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model. Variance refers to the model's sensitivity to fluctuations in the training data.

title: Comparing Bias and Variance
text: Model A has a bias squared of $$2$$ and a variance of $$12$$, while Model B has a bias squared of $$4$$ and a variance of $$1$$. Consider how these values affect the overall error of each model.

title: Total Error Calculation
text: The total error of a model can be calculated as the sum of the bias squared, variance, and irreducible error. Assume the irreducible error is the same for both models.

title: Calculate Total Error for Model A
text: Calculate the total error for Model A using the formula: total error $$=$$ bias squared + variance.

title: Calculate Total Error for Model B
text: Calculate the total error for Model B using the formula: total error $$=$$ bias squared + variance.

title: Interpreting the Results
text: Compare the total errors of Model A and Model B. Which model has a lower total error? What does this imply about the models' performances?
